text:
nina: Quick sync on dedicated pool orchestration: found two practical annoyances after running a mixed-workload replay. 1) prewarm credits get hoarded by a few noisy tenants; 2) fractional MIG reuse is noisy when we drain/attach too aggressively.

omar: can you share the replay profile? burstiness and tenant mix?

nina: 60% short (<48 tokens), 30% medium, 10% long. 12 tenants generated most of the short bursts; the rest were steady low qps. Peaks were 1.8k qps but 10s spikes.

rachel: sounds like we need two layers: per-tenant budget + pool-level recycle policy. per-tenant should decay credits over time and pool should prefer reusing partially filled MIGs before creating new ones.

omar: Agreed. Also add an admission penalty if a tenant triggered scale within last N minutes. prevents repeated micro-spikes gaming the system.

sam: proposal for policy fields (WIP):
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 1
  max_replicas: 300
  headroom_ratio: 0.15
  tenant_budget:
    default_credits: 4
    credit_decay_minutes: 20
    penalty_window_minutes: 3
  mig_reuse:
    prefer_partial: true
    reuse_threshold_percent: 35
    attach_timeout: 45s
  pool_backpressure:
    max_parallel_attaches: 3
    attach_cooldown: 90s
    emergency_throttle_percent: 0.1
```

rachel: I like prefer_partial + reuse_threshold_percent. If a MIG is >=35% utilized we should prefer scheduling hot shards there.

nina: operational question: who enforces tenant_budget? operator runtime or control-plane? If operator holds state we avoid split-brain when control-plane is flaky.

omar: operator-local enforcement wins IMO. control-plane writes intents and suggested budgets, operator maintains local credit ledger with eventual reconciliation.

devops-bot: note: recreated staging cluster with mixed-worker nodes for testing.

sam: metrics to add: tenant_credit_level, last_scale_ts, mig_partial_fill_pct. Also surface a prometheus counter for "reuse_failures" when reuse attempted but attach fails.

rachel: on attach failures - prefer a conservative fallback: allocate a small ephemeral slot (hot-slice) rather than full MIG to service latency-sensitive requests while attach completes. avoids big-cost new MIG for tiny bursts.

nina: +1, but hot-slice introduces complexity around KV cache warmup. We should tag responses with cache_warm: true so downstream can attribute latency regressions.

omar: test plan: 1) implement credit ledger + decay + penalty, 2) MIG reuse preference in allocator, 3) run 48h replay and compare cold-start rate and cost per-10k-tokens.

sam: rough SLO targets for the test: reduce cold-start p99 by 35% and keep cost delta within +15%.

rachel: UX: expose tenant_credit_level and penalty_window in console, but hide decay tuning behind expert toggle. ops will want quick knobs not YAML edits.

nina: action items: nina -> write RFC addendum with credit ledger semantics and reconciliation doc (due Tue). omar -> prototype allocator change (PR by next Fri). sam -> dashboard panels + metrics (end of week). rachel -> hot-slice design note and cache tagging (WIP).

devops-bot: integration-test: autoscaler-credit-ledger branch queued on runtime-staging.
